sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Alaska, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Saturday, October 24Passed

To get a ballot by mail, your application must be received by Saturday, October 24, 2026. To get a ballot by online delivery or fax instead, apply by 5 p.m. Alaska time on Monday, November 2, 2026. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

A mailed ballot must be postmarked on or before Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026, and must arrive within 10 days (by Friday, November 13, 2026) if mailed from inside the U.S., or within 15 days (by Wednesday, November 18, 2026) if mailed from outside the U.S. The Division suggests asking the postal clerk to hand-cancel (postmark) it at the counter. A ballot returned in person must reach a voting location by 8 p.m. on Election Day; a ballot returned by fax must be received by 8 p.m. Alaska time on Election Day. (official page)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Alaska’s own site

At school away from home, in Alaska or in another state? What Alaska says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. The Division of Elections says Alaska is a "No Excuse" voting state: anyone can apply to vote absentee by mail, fax or online delivery. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Apply on the Division of Elections' online absentee application. You need a valid Alaska driver's license or state ID. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. Fill in and sign the paper application (the signature must be handwritten; a typed or digital one is not accepted) and send it to the Absentee and Petition Office in Anchorage by mail, by fax, or by email as an attached PDF, TIFF or JPEG. You can choose to get ballots for every election in the calendar year. Open it (official page)
  • Online delivery or fax. From Monday, October 19, 2026 (15 days before Election Day), you can ask for a ballot delivered online (you print it) or by fax. The application for these must be received by 5 p.m. Alaska time on Monday, November 2, 2026. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the return envelope; you must add the postage. It must be postmarked by Election Day. (official page)
  • In person. Drop it off at any voting location by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • By fax. If you got your ballot by online delivery or fax, you can fax it back so it is received by 8 p.m. Alaska time on Election Day. Faxing means you give up a secret ballot. Ballots cannot be returned by email. (official page)

What the envelope needs

A witness is needed. Sign the return envelope (the voter certificate) in front of a witness who is 18 or older; the witness signs too. You must also give at least one identifier on the envelope; the envelope shows which kinds count. The Division suggests dating your signatures. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Alaska’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 19, 2026 to Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Early and absentee in-person voting locations open 15 days before the election, Monday, October 19, 2026, and stay open through Election Day, November 3, 2026. Each location has its own hours. At an Early Voting location your registration is checked on the spot and you scan your ballot; at an Absentee In-Person location you seal your ballot in an envelope that is reviewed later. (official page)

Where to vote early

Students

At school in Alaska, away from home

The Division says an Alaska resident at college inside or outside Alaska is a "college voter". For voting, you are an Alaska resident if you live in the state and mean to stay, or if you leave meaning to come back. The Division's pages do not say which Alaska address a student at school in another part of the state should use; its general rule is that you must have lived in the election district for at least 30 days before the election. You can ask for a ballot to be mailed to a different mailing address. (official page)

At school in another state, with Alaska as home

The Division says that when you register, update your registration, or apply for an absentee ballot while you are outside Alaska, you give the last Alaska address where you lived before you left. You stay an Alaska resident if you left meaning to return. (official page)

Military and overseas

Uniformed services members, merchant marines, commissioned corps members, their spouses and dependents, and citizens living outside the U.S. for a while use the same application, mark their military or overseas status, and choose mail, online delivery or fax. They can apply any time in the year, and ballots go out starting 45 days before Election Day. Active members and spouses do not need to intend to return to Alaska. Citizens living permanently overseas who were last living in Alaska can register as federal voters (federal races only) using the federal absentee application. A mailed ballot from outside the U.S. must be postmarked by Election Day and arrive within 15 days. (official page)

Alaska in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The receive-by dates for mailed ballots (10 days after the election from inside the U.S., 15 days from outside) come from the Division's 2026 General Election Media Packet (source 3); its absentee page gives only the postmark rule.
  • The general residency rule (live in the state meaning to stay, or leave meaning to return; 30 days in the district before the election) is on the Division's Voter Information page (source 4).
  • If you asked for a mailed ballot but decide to vote in person, the Division says you may vote at an early voting location, an absentee in-person location or your polling place, and should throw away the unvoted mailed ballot.
  • That a student can have the ballot sent to a different mailing address rests on the absentee application's ballot mailing address section, described on the Division's Absentee and Early Voting page (source 0).

How this was checked

  • Alaska's statutes and regulations (akleg.gov) answered our request with a check for human visitors, so they were not read; every fact here comes from the Division of Elections' own pages and its 2026 media packet.
  • The FVAP page loads by script and could not be read; it is linked, not quoted.
Where this comes from: 5 pages of Alaska’s election office, its laws and the federal guide

  2. Absentee and Early Voting (What to Expect) and the 2026 General Election Media Packet (dates), State of Alaska Division of Elections (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  3. Military, Overseas, and College Voters, State of Alaska Division of Elections (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  4. 2026 General Election Media Packet (election dates and FAQ), State of Alaska Division of Elections (official page; read October 21, 2026)
  5. Voter Information (registration and residency requirements), State of Alaska Division of Elections (official page; read October 21, 2026)

Checked October 21, 2026. Rules and dates can change: Alaska’s election office, and your county or local election office, have the final word.

polls:
Polls are open 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. local time. (source)

  • rest of the state: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. AKST
  • The Aleutian Islands west of 169 degrees 30 minutes west: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. HST

Anyone in line when the polls close may still vote.
